skill.name: error-sanitization
skill.description: Production-safe error handling that logs full details server-side while exposing only generic, safe messages to users. Prevents information leakage of database strings, file paths, stack traces, and API keys.

generated_query: I'm working on a FastAPI endpoint that processes file uploads. When the upload fails due to a database connection error, the raw error message includes the full database URL and credentials. In development, I want to see the detailed error for debugging, but in production I need to return only "File upload failed" to the client while logging the complete error server-side. How can I set up a reusable error handler that distinguishes between safe validation errors (which can be shown to the user) and sensitive errors (which should be hidden), and also works for batch processing where multiple files might fail with different error types?

edit_instructions.rationale: Removing the classification of validation errors and safe HTTPExceptions prevents the error handler from distinguishing safe errors from sensitive ones, which is the core requirement of the query.

        return user_message
